What Does 101.325 kPa Mean in Absolute and Gauge Pressure?

101.325 kPa is the exact value of one standard atmosphere, and it is an absolute pressure. It is measured from a perfect vacuum, so a sensor open to air at sea level under standard conditions reads 101.325 kPa absolute but 0 kPa gauge. Mixing these two references is one of the most common pressure conversion errors on a plant.

Use these two relations whenever a datasheet does not say which reference it uses:

Absolute pressure = Gauge pressure + 101.325 kPa

Gauge pressure = Absolute pressure − 101.325 kPa

ReadingAbsolute (kPa abs)Gauge (kPa g)Equivalent in atm abs
Perfect vacuum0−101.3250
Half atmosphere vacuum50.66−50.660.5
Standard sea level air101.32501
Gauge shows 100 kPa201.3251001.987
Gauge shows 200 kPa301.3252002.974
Gauge shows 1000 kPa1101.325100010.869

These conversions assume the local air pressure equals the standard 101.325 kPa. Real barometric pressure changes with weather and altitude, so precise work uses the measured local value. Gas law calculations, such as the ideal gas equation, always need absolute pressure, which is why a gauge reading must be converted first. Instrument tags often add a suffix such as kPa a or kPa g to make the reference clear.
